theater: 幼發拉底河中游基什至巴比倫河段

battle.name: 恩沙庫沙那的行動
battle.theater: 幼發拉底河中游基什至巴比倫河段
battle.brief: 恩沙庫沙那的行動是殘卷中留名的基什之王的一次中部兩河用兵。文字只留下他建埃特曼安基、供養尼普爾的記載，戰線則在基什與巴比倫之間的幼發拉底河中游展開。基什民兵以銅矛為主力長兵器，列盾陣推進；守方倚河渡與城垣。洪水之後基什王號被寫成正統，此役遂成王表與戰爭列表中最早的一條編年。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 這場衝突的交戰方有兩層。核心一方是基什王權：都城基什在幼發拉底河中游北岸、今巴比倫以北約十五公里的泰勒烏哈伊米爾，於前26至前25世紀那幾十年裡是幼發拉底河中游最有勢力的城邦之一，王號自稱「基什之王」，進而稱「四方之王」。另一方是仍在維繫古老王權的埃利都，以及同一條河上互相競爭的烏魯克、烏爾等城邦聯盟；這些城邦沒有常設政府，靠神廟經濟、水利與氏族徵發維持兵員。基什一方的軍隊骨架是城邦民兵：成年男子自備銅矛、柳條塗泥的盾與短弓，另有少量以野驢拉動的實心輪戰車，車上載持矛的貴族與護衛；指揮集中於王與神廟祭司，靠泥板、圓筒封印與份額名冊調配。後來阿卡德王朝的薩拉姆自稱「基什之王」，把基什的古老王統接到自己身上，這條正統線說明基什的用兵傳統在編年上被視為最早的正統，而不是一次孤立的衝突。
countriesEn: The opposing sides in this conflict fall into two layers. The core party is the kingship of Kish: the capital Kish lay at Tell al-Uhaymir, about fifteen kilometres north of modern Babylon on the north bank of the middle Euphrates, and through the decades between the 26th and 25th centuries BCE it was among the most powerful city-states of that river, bearing the title 'King of Kish' and, further, 'King of the Four Regions'. The other side consists of Eridu, which was still maintaining an ancient kingship, and of the rival city-state leagues of Uruk and Ur along the same river; these city-states had no standing government and kept their troops in the field through temple economies, irrigation works and clan levies. The backbone of the Kishite army was a citizen militia: adult men equipped themselves with copper spears, wicker-and-plaster shields and short bows, and a small number of solid-wheeled war wagons drawn by onagers carried spear-bearing notables and their guards. Command was concentrated in the king and the temple priesthood, and the muster, pay and rations of the army were handled on clay tablets, cylinder seals and allotment registers. Much later the Akkadian ruler Naram-Sin styled himself 'King of Kish' and tied the ancient lineage of Kish to his own house; that thread of legitimacy shows how the Kishite way of war was treated in the chronicles as the earliest lawful succession of kingship rather than as an isolated clash.
people: 關鍵人物只有一位留下名字：恩沙庫沙那，蘇美爾語作 En-šak-uš-an-na，基什第二王朝第九王。他是最早一批在王表殘卷中被記下工程功業的王：《吉施王表》殘卷（尼普爾出土）說他建起巴比倫的塔廟埃特曼安基，並供養尼普爾；後世把這位基什之王與《吉美什史诗》中因敬神而在大水中得救的洪水英雄 Ziusudra 對應起來。次要人物是記錄者：尼普爾的祭司與書吏把洪水、蘆葦束之人、黑白花斑的羊群等段落刻上泥板，使這場衝突的敘述進入後世王表；再往後，烏爾第三王朝的烏爾納姆、舒爾吉在埃特曼安基的建築銘文裡把這座塔的創建歸給更早的基什王，把前人的工程寫進自己的功業。考古史上的另一批關鍵人物是麥基，他率團在1924至1933年間主持基什皇家墓地的發掘，讓今日得以用墓中兵器、金器與象牙器重建這支軍隊的裝備與等級；1950年代尼普爾伊南納神廟出土的殘片，則是這場戰爭唯一直接指向洪水傳說的物證。
peopleEn: Only one key figure leaves a name behind: Enshakushanna, written in Sumerian as En-šak-uš-an-na, the ninth ruler of the Second Dynasty of Kish. He is among the earliest kings whose works are recorded in the fragments of a king list: the 'Kings of Kish' tablet recovered at Kish states that he built the great ziggurat Etemenanki at Babylon and provided for Nippur, and later tradition identified this king of Kish with Ziusudra, the flood-hero of the Epic of Gilgamesh who survived the great water because of his piety. The secondary figures are the recorders: the priests and scribes of Nippur cut the passages about the flood, the people of the reed bundles and the black and white spotted goats onto clay tablets, so that the narrative of this conflict entered the later king lists. Still later, Ur-Nammu and Shulgi of the Third Dynasty of Ur, in the building inscriptions of Etemenanki, assigned the founding of that terrace to an earlier king of Kish and wrote an ancestor's work into their own glory. Another set of key figures belongs to the history of archaeology: Mackay, who led the excavations of the Royal Cemetery of Kish between 1924 and 1933, allowing the equipment and rank structure of this army to be reconstructed today from the weapons, gold vessels and ivory objects of the tombs; and the fragments excavated in the 1950s from the temple of Inanna at Nippur, which remain the only material evidence pointing directly at the flood tradition of this war.
kits: 任務單這件兵器是埃及長矛：早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭以綁扎方式固定在木杆上。放在前2500年的兩河流域，它代表的是同一種技術水平下的主力長兵器——蘇美爾的城邦民兵並沒有更先進的選擇，矛與盾配合構成長矛兵的標準配備：盾遮住身體，矛尖從盾緣上方刺出，或在盾後屈身以伸出的矛尖迎擊來敵。基什一方的常備主力就是這樣一批人：手執銅矛的步兵，護以銅盔與大盾，掩體後還有以短弓射擊、用投石索拋擲石彈的同伴。戰車由野驢牽引，載著持矛的乘員與備用箭矢。攻城一方沒有攻城砲與投石機這類器械，若要取城只能靠封鎖渡口、斷糧與登牆；城防則依靠夯土城垣、護城壕與水門。銅料的來源分兩條：西南方向來自「馬干」一帶的礦區，東北方來自伊朗高原；錫料更稀，早王朝的「青銅」多為砷銅一類的銅合金，真正的錫青銅要到第三王朝之後才逐漸普及。埃及那邊的長矛同樣是銅矛，相對於同期大量出土的銅箭頭與銅刀，銅矛頭在埃及的出土數量偏少；這說明這件裝備代表的是整個早期青銅時代步兵的通用配備，而非某一族的專利。
kitsEn: The weapon assigned to this war is the Egyptian spear: an Early Dynastic spear whose copper or bronze head was lashed to a wooden shaft. Placed in the Euphrates valley of 2500 BCE it stands for the principal close-combat arm of the same technological level: the Sumerian city-state militia had no more advanced option, and the pairing of spear and shield formed the standard kit of the spearman, the shield covering the body while the point came out above the shield rim, or the fighter crouched behind the shield and answered the charge with an extended blade. The standing core of the Kishite side was exactly such men: infantry carrying copper spears, covered by copper helmets and large shields, with companions behind them shooting short bows and hurling stones from slings. War wagons were drawn by onagers and carried spear-bearing crew and spare arrows. A besieging side had no artillery in the modern sense and no siege tower or ram; to take a city it could only seal the crossings, cut supplies and climb the wall, while the defence rested on rammed-earth ramparts, a moat and water gates. Copper reached the region by two routes: from the south-west out of the mining districts of Magan, and from the north-east out of the Iranian plateau. Tin was far scarcer; 'bronze' of the Early Dynastic period was mostly a copper alloy such as arsenical copper, and true tin bronze only became common from the Third Dynasty onwards. The Egyptian spear was likewise a copper spear, and compared with the abundant copper arrowheads and knives of the same period, copper spearheads form a relatively thin group in Egypt; what this weapon represents is therefore the general equipment of Early Bronze Age infantry, not the monopoly of any single people.
tactics: 關於陣形與進攻次序，可用的文字記載極少，能確定的是三點。第一，基什的用兵建立在城邦民兵制上，戰鬥以集體列陣進行：矛兵成密集橫列，盾面朝外，弓箭手與投石手位於兩翼及後列，掩護矛鋒的推進；這是幼發拉底河谷平坦地形上唯一可行的打法，任何個人勇武都難以替代。第二，決定勝負的往往是水陸節點：基什位於河道北岸，其對手埃利都與烏魯克在南岸，渡口、灌溉渠首與通往巴比倫的航道是兵線也是補給線，奪船、築壩、截斷渡運，往往比正面衝鋒更致命。第三，攻城戰的樣式受限於器械：既無攻城塔亦無撞槌，攻方只能圍城、斷糧、堵塞水道，逼迫守方在城牆上分兵；守方則以城垣的垛口、投石與從城內放出的箭雨支援突出部。除此以外有關此戰的具體步序，史料並未留下記錄，後世把洪水歸到這位王名下，只能理解為把一次難以理解的地理災變並入王的功業，而無法據以還原戰場。合理的推論是：他的用兵成果最終體現在工程上——巴比倫的塔廟與尼普爾的渠系，說明基什在這輪衝突中握有調配勞役與物料的餘力。
tacticsEn: On formations and the order of attack the written record is extremely thin, and only three things can be stated with confidence. First, Kishite warfare rested on a city-state militia system, and combat was fought in collective order: spearmen stood in dense ranks with shield faces outward, archers and slingers holding the flanks and the rear line and covering the advance of the spearheads. In the flat terrain of the Euphrates valley this was the only workable method, and no individual valour could substitute for it. Second, what decided such contests was usually the river and road nodes: Kish sat on the north bank while its rivals Eridu and Uruk lay to the south, so the fords, the heads of the irrigation canals and the waterway to Babylon were at once lines of advance and lines of supply; taking boats, raising dams and intercepting the ferries were often more fatal than a frontal charge. Third, the shape of a siege was constrained by the available tools: with neither siege tower nor ram, the attacker could only invest the city, cut its food and block its water, forcing the defenders to spread their men along the wall, while the defenders answered with the battlements, stones and arrow-fall released from inside. Beyond these points the specific sequence of this battle survives nowhere, and the later assignment of the flood to this king's name can only be read as the folding of an incomprehensible geographical catastrophe into the credit of a king, not as a way of reconstructing the field. The reasonable inference is that the fruits of his warfare finally showed up as construction work: the terrace of Etemenanki at Babylon and the canal system at Nippur show that Kish had the surplus to allocate labour and materials during this round of conflict.
data: 可以核對的數字有限，且多為考古與地理測量值。基什在泰勒烏哈伊米爾，約北緯32.55度、東經45.38度；巴比倫在泰勒巴比倫，約北緯32.53度、東經44.40度，兩地相距約十五公里；尼普爾在努法爾，約北緯32.0度、東經44.3度，位於埃爾代姆與幼發拉底兩水交會處；烏魯克在瓦爾卡，約北緯31.3度、東經45.6度；埃利都在阿比同比河入海口一帶，約北緯30.8度、東經47.7度；烏爾在埃爾代姆與幼發拉底之間，約北緯30.96度、東經46.1度。年代上，戰爭列表把這場衝突繫於前2500年，而基什第二王朝的通行的學界推定落在前26至前25世紀，兩者相合，偏差不大。埃特曼安基的規模：後來第三王朝重建的塔基約九十米見方，通行說法稱其總高約七十米上下，銘文把塔名與「天之門」的意象連在一起。王表給這位王的統治年限遠長於任何可接受的常規，學界普遍視為編年上的誇大。基什皇家墓地自1924年起陸續挖掘，墓葬以百計，其中出土的銅盔是已知最早的一批金屬頭盔之一。烏爾王墓區另有一層被稱為「洪水層」的淤積，年代學家常拿它作為早王朝末期至阿卡德時期的斷代標尺，可與《吉施王表》的洪水段落互相對照。銅料自西南的馬干與東北的伊朗高原輸入，錫料遠比銅稀少，早王朝的青銅多為砷銅。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked are few, and most of them are archaeological or geographical measurements. Kish lay at Tell al-Uhaymir, roughly 32.55 degrees north and 45.38 degrees east; Babylon at Tell Babil, roughly 32.53 north and 44.40 east, about fifteen kilometres downstream from Kish; Nippur at Nuffar, roughly 32.0 north and 44.3 east, at the meeting of the Adum and the Euphrates; Uruk at Warka, roughly 31.3 north and 45.6 east; Eridu near the mouth of the Abū Zab, roughly 30.8 north and 47.7 east; Ur between the Adum and the Euphrates, roughly 30.96 north and 46.1 east. As to date, the list of wars files this clash under 2500 BCE, while the standard scholarly placement of the Second Dynasty of Kish falls in the 26th to 25th centuries BCE; the two agree closely. On the size of Etemenanki: the terrace rebuilt under the Third Dynasty of Ur was roughly ninety metres square, the usual figure for its total height is around seventy metres, and the inscriptions tie the name of the terrace to the image of a gate to heaven. The reign length the king list assigns to this king is far longer than any acceptable norm and is generally treated by scholars as chronological inflation. The Royal Cemetery of Kish was excavated from 1924 onward and yielded a count of tombs running into the hundreds, among them a copper helmet belonging to the earliest group of metal helmets known. In the royal cemetery of Ur there is further a layer of silt called the flood layer, which chronologists commonly use as a benchmark for the end of the Early Dynastic and the Akkadian periods and which can be compared with the flood passage of the 'Kings of Kish' tablet. Copper came in from Magan to the south-west and from the Iranian plateau to the north-east; tin was far scarcer than copper, and Early Dynastic bronze was for the most part arsenical copper.
cause: 打起嚟的理由可以從結構上看：三件東西在同一段河谷裡同時被爭奪——水、耕地與神廟。基什的位置在幼發拉底河中游，握有橫跨東西的渡口與運河樞紐，向西可直達埃利都這座古老的王朝發祥地，向南沿埃爾代姆河通往烏魯克與烏爾這兩座正在上升的城邦；前2600年前後，這些城邦各自完成王權與聖殿體系的成形，彼此的農田靠同一套灌渠網維生，任何一方擴張都直接改變水量分配。直接導火很可能是航道與渡口：基什要在下游建起巴比倫的塔廟埃特曼安基，就必須調動大量勞役、木料與銅料，並在河上維持船隊航線，而下游的埃利都與烏魯克不願坐看基什控制下游水道與信仰中心。另一層起因是名分：基什的王號要自稱「四方之王」，就得在實力上壓過周邊城邦；而王表把這一切收束在「建塔、供養尼普爾」的記載裡，說明對當代人而言，衝突的終點不是佔地，而是取得主持神廟與分配水源的權力。至於洪水，它可能不是原因，而是壓力：一次淹沒大地的大水之後，秩序與人口都要重新編排，強者得以藉救災與重建的組織能力壯大，這正好解釋了為何洪水與王的功業在同一段文字裡並列。
causeEn: The reason for the fighting can be read off the structure: three things were contested at once in the same stretch of river valley — water, farmland and temples. Kish sat on the middle Euphrates holding the fords and the canal hubs that ran east and west; to the west lay Eridu, the ancient seat of kingship, and to the south, down the Adum, the rising city-states of Uruk and Ur. Around 2600 BCE each of these polities had completed the shaping of its kingship and temple system, their fields sustained by a single network of irrigation canals, so that the expansion of any one of them directly altered the distribution of water. The immediate trigger was most likely the waterways and the crossings: to raise the terrace of Etemenanki at Babylon downstream, Kish had to move large numbers of labourers, timber and copper and keep a shipping line open on the river, and Eridu and Uruk downstream were unwilling to watch Kish take control of the lower waterway and of the religious centre. A second cause was precedence: for the title 'King of the Four Regions' to mean anything, Kish had to outweigh the neighbouring city-states in actual force. The king list closes the whole business into the single line about building the terrace and providing for Nippur, which shows that for the people of the time the point of the conflict was not acreage but the right to preside over the temples and to apportion the water. As for the flood, it was probably not the cause but the pressure: after the great water covered the land, order and population had to be reorganised, and the strong grew by organising relief and rebuilding, which is exactly why the flood and the king's achievement stand side by side in the same passage.
impact: 這場衝突的後續影響，見於三條線索。第一是王權正統：基什第二王朝在編年上被排在烏魯克之前，後來阿卡德王朝的薩拉姆自稱「基什之王」，把基什當作自身王統的源頭，說明這輪城邦之間的角力被當成王權合法性的起點；再往後，烏爾的第三王朝又把埃特曼安基的創建歸給這位基什之王，把前人的工程寫進自己的功業。第二是城市的地位：巴比倫從此在幼發拉底河東岸坐實了宗教中心的角色，這座塔廟最終在帕提亞與塞琉古時期被拆去用作他城建材，又在近代的考古發掘中重新出土，兩河流域宗教地理的骨架因而被固定下來。第三是敘事與文字：洪水段落連同「蘆葦束之人」「黑白花斑山羊」的說法被抄入王表殘卷，日後成為《吉美什史诗》洪水母題的源頭之一；而記錄這些的泥板、圓筒封印與份額名冊，也把蘇美爾的行政技術往前推了一大步。此外，前2500年前後基什能夠承擔那樣規模的工程與用兵，本身說明它已是一個具備財政與勞役調配能力的城邦國家，之後兩河流域「王之王」的自稱傳統，多半是在這樣的基礎上長成。
impactEn: The consequences of this clash show along three threads. The first is royal legitimacy: the Second Dynasty of Kish is placed in the chronicles before Uruk, and the Akkadian ruler Naram-Sin later styled himself 'King of Kish', treating Kish as the source of his own line; that means the rivalry between these city-states was remembered as the starting point of legitimate kingship. Later still, the Third Dynasty of Ur assigned the founding of Etemenanki to this king of Kish and wrote an ancestor's work into its own glory. The second is the standing of the city: Babylon from then on held the role of religious centre on the east bank of the Euphrates; the terrace was eventually dismantled in the Parthian and Seleucid periods for use as building material in other cities, and was re-excavated in modern times, so that the skeleton of the religious geography of Mesopotamia was fixed in place. The third is narrative and writing: the flood passage, together with the sayings of the 'people of the reed bundles' and the 'black and white spotted goats', was copied into the fragments of the king list and later became one of the sources of the flood motif in the Epic of Gilgamesh, while the clay tablets, cylinder seals and allotment registers that recorded all this pushed Sumerian administrative technique a long step forward. In addition, the fact that Kish could carry construction and campaigning on that scale around 2500 BCE shows that it had already become a city-state with the fiscal and labour-allocation capacity to do so, and the later tradition in Mesopotamia of calling a king 'King of the Four Regions' grew largely out of such a base.
result: 結局無法用戰役報告的方式陳述：沒有戰報，沒有陣亡名冊，連是否真正交戰都無法斷定。可以確定的是三點。第一，基什一系在編年上取得了「王之王」的位置，恩沙庫沙那被記成建起埃特曼安基並供養尼普爾的那位王，這條記載在他本人的年代裡就已定形，往後不斷被引用，取代了對戰役細節的記錄。第二，烏魯克與埃利都作為舊王權中心的相對地位下降：基什把王號寫成四方之王，又在下游握有神廟與航道的組織能力，洪水年代的蘇美爾再也沒有回到那種由單一城邦統合兩河的格局，直到阿卡德王朝才重新出現。第三，洪水敘事被寫成恩沙庫沙那功業的一部分，這種把大水解釋為王者德行之驗證的敘事方式，成為此後兩河流域王權敘事的定型；從烏爾納姆、舒爾吉到嗣後的亞述與巴比倫君主，每一位都把治水、重建與正統繫在一起。若以戰爭列表的標準衡量，這場戰爭留下的並非勝負，而是名分：一座塔廟、一段洪水，加上一條從基什通向嗣後美索不達米亞王權的線索。裝備面同樣留下痕跡——銅矛這類早期青銅時代步兵的標準長兵器，在嗣後數百年的兩河流域步兵中延續使用，直到鐵兵器普及才退居次要。
resultEn: The outcome cannot be stated in the manner of a battle report: there is no despatch, no casualty roll, and not even a certainty that fighting took place. Three things can be said. First, the Kishite line took the position of king of kings in the chronicles; Enshakushanna is recorded as the king who built Etemenanki and provided for Nippur, and that notice had already taken shape in his own lifetime and was cited again and again afterwards, replacing any record of the details of the fighting. Second, the relative standing of Uruk and Eridu as old centres of kingship declined: Kish wrote its title as king of the four regions, and it organised the temples and the waterway on the lower river, and the Sumer of the flood era never regained the pattern of a single city-state uniting the two rivers, until the Akkadian dynasty re-established it. Third, the flood narrative was written into part of Enshakushanna's achievement; this way of reading the great water as proof of the ruler's virtue became the fixed formula of Mesopotamian kingship narrative, from Ur-Nammu and Shulgi to the later Assyrian and Babylonian monarchs, each of whom tied water control, rebuilding and legitimacy together. Measured by the standard of a list of wars, what this conflict left behind was not a victory or a defeat but a precedence: a terrace, a flood, and a thread running from Kish to the later kingship of Mesopotamia. The equipment leaves a mark as well — the copper spear, the standard close-combat arm of Early Bronze Age infantry, kept its place in the Mesopotamian foot soldier for the following centuries, and only fell back to a secondary role once iron weapons spread.
